# Temple Scroll Column 12 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 12 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 12:3 — "afflict your souls" vs. "afflict yourselves" vs. "deny yourselves"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall afflict your souls" | Literal ve-innitem et nafshoteikhem; preserves "soul" (nefesh) |
| LOGOS | "you shall afflict yourselves" | Standard rendering; nefesh here is reflexive, not a separate entity |
| PNEUMA | "you must deny yourselves" | "Deny" captures the practical meaning (fasting, abstention) |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "afflict yourselves" (LOGOS), consistent with the project's Leviticus ruling (ve-innitem = "you shall afflict yourselves"). EMET's "souls" imports a body-soul dualism foreign to Hebrew anthropology. PNEUMA's "deny" is interpretive — the Hebrew root 'innah means "to afflict," not merely "to deny."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Consistent with established project convention.

---

## 12:4 — scope of work prohibition — "all work" vs. "no manner of work" vs. "any work at all"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all work you shall not do" | Literal with Hebrew word order |
| LOGOS | "You shall do no manner of work" | Formal; "no manner of" emphasizes total prohibition |
| PNEUMA | "You must not do any work at all" | Natural emphatic English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Yom Kippur work prohibition is stricter than the standard festival prohibition (kol melakhah vs. melekhet avodah) — "no manner of work" captures this absolute quality. EMET's inverted syntax is awkward in English.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 12:6 — karet formula — "soul that does not afflict itself" vs. "person"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "every soul that does not afflict itself" | Literal kol ha-nefesh asher lo te'unneh |
| LOGOS | "every person who does not practice self-denial" | "Person" for nefesh in legal context; "practice self-denial" for clarity |
| PNEUMA | "anyone who does not practice self-denial" | Simplest, most natural phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "every person who does not afflict themselves" — combining LOGOS's "person" (correct for legal nefesh) with the established "afflict" verb rather than LOGOS's "self-denial" paraphrase. Maintains consistency with 12:3.

**Status:** Resolved with compromise.

---

## 12:13 — "sin offering of the atonements" vs. "sin offering of atonement" vs. "special sin offering"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sin offering of the atonements" | Literal chattat ha-kippurim; preserves plural |
| LOGOS | "sin offering of atonement" | Standard rendering; English does not pluralize "atonement" in this context |
| PNEUMA | "special sin offering for atonement" | "Special" clarifies distinction from the standard goat |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "sin offering of atonement" (LOGOS). The plural kippurim is a Hebrew intensive/abstract plural, not a true plural; English "atonement" already conveys the concept. PNEUMA's "special" is an interpretive addition not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 12:16 — "statute forever" vs. "perpetual statute" vs. "lasting requirement"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a statute forever in all your dwelling places" | Literal chuqqat olam |
| LOGOS | "a perpetual statute in all your dwelling places" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "a lasting requirement wherever you live" | Accessible rephrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. Consistent with Column 11 ruling on chuqqat olam. "Perpetual statute" maintains legal register.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Consistent with Column 11 precedent.

---
